rows.grounds: Refers to the teaching or scripture of Svāyambhuva; genitive qualifying the subject matter being explained.
Fused expression: jaḍatām (inertness, accusative) qualified by anādikām (beginningless), governed by infinitive apanetum (to remove).
Dative of benefit; refers to bound individual selves (aṇu) for whom the removal is intended.

items.question: For what purpose is the teaching of the Svāyambhuva presented to individual selves?
premises: Individual selves are affected by beginningless inertness.
The teaching of the Svāyambhuva aims at removing that inertness.
The exposition is directed for the benefit of individual selves.
items.inference: Therefore, the Svāyambhuva teaching is presented to remove the beginningless inertness of individual selves.
uncertainties: Whether svāyambhuvasya refers specifically to the Svāyambhuvāgama or more generally to a self-born teaching is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: The teaching of the Svāyambhuva is presented in order to remove the beginningless inertness of individual selves.

rows.grounds: Instrumental indicating the manner of presentation.
Passive verb indicating that the subject matter is being taught or set forth.
Concluding particle marking the end of the statement or exposition.

items.question: In what manner is this doctrinal teaching being set forth?
premises: The teaching is being formally explained.
The mode of explanation is brevity.
The particle iti marks the conclusion of this presentation.
items.inference: Therefore, the doctrinal teaching is concluded as having been explained briefly.
items.plain_english: Thus, it is explained in brief.
